title: Storage and Database Selection: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Storage and Database Selection: Visual Guide

1. Five Workload Axes | the bridge from OLTP-vs-OLAP to five dials (structure, access, scale, latency, distribution) that resolve to a named GCP service, plus an 'analysts also run aggregates' toggle and the IoT-fleet preset | the matrix is a procedure, and it frequently outputs TWO services connected by a pipeline rather than one

2. The Relational Ladder | three escalation requirements toggled against Cloud SQL, AlloyDB and Spanner, each rung marked FITS or RULED OUT with its reason, plus the payments-ledger and Belgium-inventory presets | Cloud SQL and AlloyDB scale writes vertically in one region; only the co-occurrence of relational + global + strong consistency justifies Spanner

3. Three NoSQL Centers | four pieces of one RAG chat product routed to Firestore, Bigtable or Memorystore, with a slider for how many rows or documents a single query returns | Firestore bills per document operation (10,000 documents = 10,000 reads), Bigtable's row key IS the query, and Memorystore is never a system of record

4. The Temperature Ladder | a re-reads-per-year slider costing 10 TB as Standard vs Nearline, plus an object-age slider running the age 30/90/365 lifecycle policy and its early-deletion minimums | every class shares 11 nines of durability, so the axis is access frequency: Nearline break-even is monthly re-reads, and deleting a Coldline object at day 10 bills 90

5. Choosing The Mover | volume, network capacity, freshness and destination set as four dials, with the live bytes x 8 / bps arithmetic, selecting DMS, Datastream, DTS, Transfer Appliance or Storage Transfer Service | DMS ends with the source retired while Datastream runs forever; 1 PB over 1 Gbps is ~93 days of saturated line, which is the whole case for the appliance
